subject: Operations
title: Takata Airbag Recall
description: A quick, practical guide to Takata Airbag Recall.

hook.text: An airbag meant to save your life fires metal shrapnel at you. Takata's defective airbags killed 27 people worldwide.

buildup.text: Takata used ammonium nitrate as a propellant—it was cheaper but degraded in heat and humidity over time.

discovery.text: The propellant became unstable and caused inflators to rupture violently instead of deploying the airbag safely.

twist.text: Takata knew about the defect for years but concealed test data and resisted recalls to protect its business.

climax.text: The recall covered 67 million vehicles—the largest automotive recall in history. Takata went bankrupt in 2017.

punchline.text: Covering up a defect cost more than fixing it ever would have.

quiz.question: Why did Takata's airbag inflators fail?
options: The propellant degraded in heat and humidity
